=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .github/workflows/clarify.yml:`if:` condition for `issue_comment` | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The command logic (`startsWith('/reclarify')` OR `(contains('\n/reclarify') AND NO_MARKER)`) fails to check for automation markers when `/reclarify` is on the first line. A comment starting with `/reclarify` but containing an automation marker will incorrectly trigger clarification.
  WHY: An automation-generated comment that starts with `/reclarify` will trigger the `clarify` job, potentially creating infinite loops or interfering with orchestrator state, violating the requirement that automation-marker comments must never trigger.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`_rc_is_command` logic within `_rc_body_lc` | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The logic `if [[ "${_rc_first}" == /reclarify* ]] || { ... }` checks for the automation marker only if the command is on a later line. A first-line command bypasses the marker check.
  WHY: Same as above; an automation-generated comment starting with `/reclarify` will trigger the reclarify logic.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:`is_reclarify_command_body` | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The implementation allows `text.startswith("/reclarify")` without checking `text` for automation markers.
  WHY: The orchestrator's processing logic is susceptible to triggering on automation comments starting with `/reclarify`.
- Requirement: “Comments carrying an automation marker (`<!-- ai:… -->`) must never trigger,” and tests must cover an automation comment that does not trigger.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/clarify.yml`, `.github/workflows/internal-clarify.yml`, `workflow-templates/ai-clarify.yml`, `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py`, and `tests/test_phase_wrapper_predicate_contract.py`.
  Evidence of absence: The predicates and classifiers bypass the automation-marker check when `/reclarify` is at the start of the comment. `tests/test_phase_wrapper_predicate_contract.py` (case `RECLARIFY_CASES`) explicitly expects marker-bearing first-line commands to return `True`, which directly contradicts the safety requirement.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- Requirement: "comments carrying an automation marker (`<!-- ai:… -->`) [must] never trigger" (from linked issue #6630 / original #5243, "Guard against self-triggering" section, bullet 1).
  Expected change site: the three classifier implementations plus the predicates — `is_reclarify_command_body` in `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:3802-3815`, the bash classifier blocks in `.github/workflows/clarify.yml:441-454` and `.github/workflows/clarify.yml:1605-1617`, the `RECLARIFY_COMMAND_JQ_DEF` filter in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:23`, and the `contains(...'<!-- ai:')` sub-clause inside the job predicates in `.github/workflows/clarify.yml:21`, `.github/workflows/internal-clarify.yml:17`, and `workflow-templates/ai-clarify.yml:16`.
  Evidence of absence: every classifier keeps the `<!-- ai:` exclusion behind the *later-line* branch only. `text.startswith("/reclarify")` returns True regardless of any `<!-- ai:` marker in the body, and `tests/test_phase_wrapper_predicate_contract.py:116-117` pins `("/reclarify [auto-requeued-by-poller]\n<!-- ai:reclarify-replay:v1 source=1 -->", True)` and `("/reclarify\n<!-- ai:security-dependency-released:7 -->", True)` as expected positives, confirming the lenient behaviour is the contract. The autofix PR comment acknowledges the gap ("Ignored suggestions") and leaves it open for compatibility with the poller replay sweep and the security-dependency release; `agents.md:60-72` documents the lenient behaviour as intentional ("marker-bearing automation comments ... restart clarify only when the command is on their first line"). The issue spec, however, lists the marker exclusion as one of two hard guards against self-triggering.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- Requirement: "Comments carrying an automation marker (`<!-- ai:… -->`) must never trigger," and tests must cover an automation comment that does not trigger.
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/clarify.yml:21`, `.github/workflows/internal-clarify.yml:19`, `workflow-templates/ai-clarify.yml:19`, `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:is_reclarify_command_body`, `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:RECLARIFY_COMMAND_JQ_DEF`, and `tests/test_phase_wrapper_predicate_contract.py:RECLARIFY_CASES`
  Evidence of absence: The job predicates' `startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/reclarify')` branch bypasses the automation-marker exclusions (`!contains(..., '<!-- ai:')`), so a first-line `/reclarify` in a marker-bearing automation comment still triggers clarification. `is_reclarify_command_body` in `scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:3813-3820` and `RECLARIFY_COMMAND_JQ_DEF` in `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:23-25` apply the same logic. `tests/test_phase_wrapper_predicate_contract.py:107-108` explicitly expects marker-bearing first-line commands to return `True` (`("/reclarify [auto-requeued-by-poller]\n<!-- ai:reclarify-replay:v1 source=1 -->", True)` and `("/reclarify\n<!-- ai:security-dependency-released:7 -->", True)`), so the requested automation-comment negative test case is not implemented. The linked issue explicitly requires that automation markers never trigger and asks for a test covering this case, but the implementation preserves backward compatibility for two existing flows (poller replay sweep and security-dependency release) that post first-line `/reclarify` with markers. The editor's summary acknowledges this deviation and explains the rationale, but the issue specification is absolute: "comments carrying an automation marker must never trigger." If the stricter rule is required, the existing flows need an alternative mechanism to restart clarification.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
